User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the PISA VIBE online store.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

registrationDate.description: Date and time when the user registered.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a product (e.g., shoes, clothing) available in the PISA VIBE store.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

category.description: Category of the product (e.g., shoes, clothing).

quality.description: The quality tier of the product.

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents an order placed by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

orderDate.description: Date and time when the order was placed.

status.description: Status of the order (e.g., pending, processing, shipped, delivered).

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents an item within an order.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrderItem entity.

quantity.description: Quantity of the product in the order item.

itemPrice.description: Price of the item (price per unit).

Recommendation.title: Recommendation
Recommendation.description: Represents a product recommendation for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Recommendation entity.

recommendationDate.description: Date and time when the product was recommended.

score.description: Relevance score of the recommendation (e.g., based on AI model output).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the PISA VIBE online store, focusing on products, orders, user data, and personalized recommendations. The structure prioritizes security, scalability, and ease of debugging, adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation. Key aspects of the design are: 

1.  **Authorization Independence:** The design avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies to ensure atomic operations (transactions/batches) are not compromised. The security rules rely on `request.auth.uid` and data stored within the documents themselves rather than retrieving parent document data.

2.  **Structural Segregation:** The structure ensures all documents within a collection share the same security requirements. For example, user-specific data is stored under the `/users/{userId}` path.

3.  **Access Modeling:**
    *   **User Data:** User profiles are stored in `/users/{userId}`. This path-based ownership ensures that only the user can access their profile data.
    *   **Orders:** Orders are stored under `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}`, continuing the hierarchical path for user-owned data. This allows easy enforcement of ownership-based security rules.
    *   **Order Items:** Order items are nested under orders at `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}/order_items/{orderItemId}`.
    *   **Recommendations:** Recommendations are stored under `/users/{userId}/recommendations/{recommendationId}`. This follows the same pattern as orders and other user-specific data.
    *   **Products:** Product data is stored in a top-level `/products` collection, allowing for easy listing and querying of all products.

4. **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
    *   The segregation of user-specific data into subcollections enables secure `list` operations. For example, listing orders is performed within the user's own document scope, preventing unauthorized access to other users' orders.

5.  **Data Clarity:** Using consistent naming conventions (e.g., `userId`, `productId`) and an explicit `status` field for orders enhances predictability and debuggability.
